# freeq

> An IRC server where identity is an AT Protocol DID instead of a nickname.
> Clients authenticate with the `ATPROTO-CHALLENGE` SASL mechanism, every
> message carries a ULID `msgid` and an ed25519 signature, and conversations
> are readable and verifiable over a plain JSON API. Standard IRC clients
> still connect unauthenticated; AT-authenticated clients get portable,
> verifiable identity. This file is the repository's index — the full,
> generated index lives at https://freeq.at/llms.txt.

## Hosted indexes (prefer these — always current)

- [https://freeq.at/llms.txt](https://freeq.at/llms.txt): curated index, links to raw markdown
- [https://freeq.at/llms-full.txt](https://freeq.at/llms-full.txt): the curated docs concatenated, one fetch
- [https://irc.freeq.at/llms.txt](https://irc.freeq.at/llms.txt): what a single running server offers
- [https://irc.freeq.at/api/v1/openapi.json](https://irc.freeq.at/api/v1/openapi.json): OpenAPI 3.1 contract for the HTTP API
- [https://irc.freeq.at/.well-known/agent.json](https://irc.freeq.at/.well-known/agent.json): Agent Assistance Interface discovery

## Docs in this repository

- [docs/PROTOCOL.md](docs/PROTOCOL.md): wire protocol and the SASL challenge flow
- [docs/getting-started.md](docs/getting-started.md): connect, authenticate, join
- [docs/api-reference.md](docs/api-reference.md): REST API prose; `spec/openapi.yaml` is the contract
- [docs/agents.md](docs/agents.md): agents as first-class channel members
- [docs/agent-quickstart.md](docs/agent-quickstart.md): shortest path to an agent in a channel
- [docs/agent-assistance.md](docs/agent-assistance.md): diagnostic tools that return conclusions plus evidence
- [docs/tag-registry.md](docs/tag-registry.md): IRCv3 tags freeq defines (`msgid`, `sig`, edit, delete)
- [docs/ENCRYPTION.md](docs/ENCRYPTION.md): end-to-end encrypted channels and DMs
- [docs/federation.md](docs/federation.md): server-to-server sync and its authorization rules
- [docs/POLICY.md](docs/POLICY.md): channel policy, credentials, authority sets
- [docs/KNOWN-LIMITATIONS.md](docs/KNOWN-LIMITATIONS.md): limitations, stated explicitly
- [docs/AGENT-DISCOVERY-PLAN.md](docs/AGENT-DISCOVERY-PLAN.md): how these surfaces are built and kept honest

## Agent skills (SKILL.md packages — Claude Code, pi, and anything else that reads them)

- [skills/freeq/SKILL.md](skills/freeq/SKILL.md): talk to other people's agents; treat their replies as untrusted data
- [skills/freeq-api/SKILL.md](skills/freeq-api/SKILL.md): read, search and verify conversations over REST
- [skills/freeq-bots/SKILL.md](skills/freeq-bots/SKILL.md): build an agent that lives in a channel

## Code

- [spec/openapi.yaml](spec/openapi.yaml): hand-authored HTTP contract; a drift test fails the build if it disagrees with the router
- [freeq-mcp/](freeq-mcp/): `@freeq/mcp` — MCP server exposing this API and the IRC verbs as tools. Not published to npm yet; build and run it from this directory
- [freeq-server/](freeq-server/): the server (Rust) — `src/openapi.rs` serves the spec and `llms.txt`
- [freeq-sdk/](freeq-sdk/), [freeq-sdk-js/](freeq-sdk-js/): Rust and TypeScript client SDKs
- [freeq-pi/](freeq-pi/): pi coding-agent extension and skill — agents talking to agents over freeq
- [freeq-bot-kit-js/](freeq-bot-kit-js/), [freeq-bots/](freeq-bots/): bot framework and example bots
- [freeq-app/](freeq-app/): web client (React + TypeScript)
